globalConstraints.text: Preserve generalized-role versus concrete-realization discipline. `DOKĄD`, `SKĄD`, and `GDZIE` are not new architecture types or proof of exclusive preposition government.
Keep alternative schemas alternative; never reconstruct an unsupported maximal frame.
Preserve lexical `się` and `sobie` as part of the verified identity.
Preserve required lexical `udział` in `brać udział w + Locative` and `wziąć udział w + Locative`.
Never transfer syntax through an aspect metadata relationship.
Keep ordinary Genitive under negation grammar-owned rather than creating a lemma-specific lexical pattern.
Preserve exact clause distinctions: `że`, `żeby`, interrogative-dependent, and direct speech.
Keep related identities separate, including `radzić / radzić sobie`, `uczyć / uczyć się`, and reflexive/non-reflexive entries.
Do not restore any rejected Phase 2 hypothesis during authoring.
Allocate no stable ID until the exact Phase 4 editorial record is approved under the later ID policy.

bindingConstraints.text: Author only the production sense with nad + Instrumental. Do not encode jako + Nominative or ordinary workplace GDZIE as a verb pattern.

meanings.internalScope: Goal-directed work on creating or producing something. Excludes employment, occupation, workplace, beneficiary, collaboration, and work-with-person readings.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For creating or developing something, use nad + Instrumental: pracuję nad filmem (I'm working on a film).

examples.en: I am working on a new film.

bindingConstraints.text: The locked product can encode individual do/na realizations but not the generalized DOKĄD alternation as one abstract slot; later authoring must avoid implying exclusive government.

meanings.internalScope: Directed motion on foot, including going in order to perform an action. The destination forms are individual realizations of a selected destination role, not an exhaustive government list.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey on foot, do + Genitive is one common way to name the destination; other destinations use other prepositions.
For this journey on foot, na + Accusative is another way to name the destination; it does not replace other destination prepositions.
Use an infinitive to say the action you are going to do: idę kupić chleb (I'm going to buy bread).

examples.en: I am going to the shop.
I am going to the swimming pool.
I am going to buy bread.

bindingConstraints.text: The semantic boundary between event attendance na CO and a spatial na-destination must be enforced during later sense selection.

meanings.internalScope: Habitual attendance at an activity or institution. The na + Accusative pattern is for the activity or attendance reading, not a merely spatial na-destination.
Repeated or habitual motion on foot to a place or in order to do an action. Keeps the selected destination and infinitive purpose separate from attendance/activity na + Accusative.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For a regular activity or class, use na + Accusative: chodzę na kurs polskiego (I go to a Polish course). This is not just a spatial destination.
For regular trips on foot, do + Genitive can name a selected destination; other destination prepositions are possible in other contexts.
Use an infinitive to say the activity you go to do regularly: chodzę pływać (I go swimming).

examples.en: I go to a Polish course.
I go to the library regularly.

bindingConstraints.text: Walenty could not be inspected at lemma level, so the unexpected selected-vehicle result lacks independent corroboration and deserves reviewer attention.

meanings.internalScope: Directed travel using a vehicle, animal, or transport or sport equipment. Destination and selected vehicle/equipment constructions are separate patterns; route, time, and ordinary manner are excluded.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey by transport, do + Genitive is one way to name the selected destination; it is not the only possible destination preposition.
When you name the vehicle, use the bare Instrumental: jadę autobusem (I'm travelling by bus). In this sense it names the selected vehicle for the journey.
Use na + Locative for travel on a vehicle or piece of equipment: jadę na rowerze (I'm travelling by bicycle).

bindingConstraints.text: As with jechać, independent lemma-level Walenty corroboration was unavailable; exact pedagogical delimitation of vehicle participant versus manner needs review.

meanings.internalScope: Repeated or habitual overland travel using transport. Frequency is part of the meaning but is not a complement; destination and selected vehicle/equipment constructions are separate patterns.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For repeated travel by transport, do + Genitive can name a selected destination; other destination prepositions are possible in other contexts.
When you name the vehicle for repeated travel, use the bare Instrumental: jeżdżę tramwajem (I travel by tram). This is a selected vehicle pattern, not a frequency pattern.
Use na + Locative for repeated travel on a vehicle or piece of equipment: jeżdżę na nartach (I go skiing).

glossesEn: arrive at a truth or conviction
meanings.internalScope: The abstract intellectual-result sense of reaching a thought, truth, conclusion, or conviction. Excludes literal walking destinations and other dojść senses.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching a conclusion or truth, use do + Genitive: dojść do wniosku (reach a conclusion). This is not about physically walking somewhere.

bindingConstraints.text: The selected-vehicle analysis should receive independent review because it reverses the Phase 2 working suspicion and Walenty was inaccessible.

glossesEn: get to a destination by vehicle
meanings.internalScope: Reaching an endpoint through travel in or on transport. Concrete do and na endpoint forms are individual realizations of the selected endpoint role; vehicle and equipment constructions remain separate.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching an endpoint by transport, do + Genitive is one way to name it; it is not the only possible endpoint preposition.
For reaching an endpoint by transport, na + Accusative is another way to name it; other endpoint prepositions are possible.
When you name the vehicle used to reach the endpoint, use the bare Instrumental: dojadę pociągiem (I'll get there by train).
Use na + Locative for reaching the endpoint on a vehicle or piece of equipment: dojedziemy na rowerach (we'll get there by bicycle).

examples.en: We will get to the hotel.
We will get to the station.
I will get there by train.
We will get there by bicycle.

bindingConstraints.text: Label do/z forms as goal/source realizations, never as exclusive government; keep the imperfective evidence independent from wrócić.

meanings.internalScope: Imperfective return to a place previously occupied. The do and z forms are concrete realizations of selected return-goal and return-source positions, not exclusive government.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this return meaning, do + Genitive can express the place you return to. It is one realization of the return goal, not the only form.
For this return meaning, z + Genitive can express the place you return from. It is one realization of the return source, not the only form.

examples.en: I am returning to the flat.
I am coming back from the cinema.

bindingConstraints.text: Label do/z as realizations, preserve the moderate independent-slot signal, and do not inherit syntax from wracać.

meanings.internalScope: Bounded perfective return to a place previously occupied. This independently evidenced meaning uses concrete do and z realizations of selected return-goal and return-source positions, not exclusive government.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this completed return, do + Genitive can express the place you return to. It is one realization of the return goal, not the only form.
For this completed return, z + Genitive can express the place you return from. It is one realization of the return source, not the only form.

examples.en: I will return to the flat.
I came back from the cinema.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep event/activity and place readings sense-specific; label concrete destinations as realizations and do not author an unverified person-target do frame.

meanings.internalScope: Literal arrival at a place. The do + Genitive form is a concrete realization of a selected destination role; this record excludes person-specific targets.
One-off arrival in order to perform or undergo an activity or event. Keeps event/activity na + Accusative and the selected infinitive separate from literal place arrival and arrival time.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For literal arrival at a place, do + Genitive can name the destination; it is one way to express that destination.
For a one-off event or activity, na + Accusative can name the destination: przyszliśmy na koncert (we came to a concert).
Use an infinitive to say the one-off action you came to do: przyszedłem odebrać dokument (I came to collect a document).

examples.en: I came to collect a document.

bindingConstraints.text: Author do/na only as destination realizations, not exclusive government; exclude source, vehicle, route, and time from the lexical pattern.

meanings.internalScope: Arrival at a destination by travelling in or on transport. do+Genitive and na+Accusative are individual realizations of a selected destination role, not exhaustive government. Excludes source, vehicle, route, time, and manner; no syntax is borrowed from imperfective przyjeżdżać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to express this destination is do + Genitive: przyjadę do Warszawy (I'll arrive in Warsaw).
Another common way to express this destination is na + Accusative: przyjadę na dworzec (I'll arrive at the station).

examples.en: I will arrive at the station.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep literal exit separate from sport/result meanings and label every concrete source/destination form as a generalized-role realization.

meanings.internalScope: Literal exit from a bounded place. z+Genitive realizes a selected source role; do+Genitive and na+Accusative realize a selected destination role. All are non-exclusive realizations. Excludes the separately evidenced ranking/result sense (na+Accusative, e.g. 'wyjść na prowadzenie'), which is not authored in this record; also excludes route, time, and manner. No syntax is borrowed from imperfective wychodzić.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For the place you are leaving, use z + Genitive: wyszedłem z domu (I left the house).
One common way to name where you're going after leaving is do + Genitive: wyjdę do ogrodu (I'll go out to the garden).
Another common way to name that destination is na + Accusative: wyjdę na balkon (I'll go out onto the balcony).

examples.en: I will go out to the garden.
I will go out onto the balcony.

bindingConstraints.text: Author only the source-role realization; do not add destination, vehicle, route, or time frames and do not imply exclusive z government.

glossesEn: depart from a place by vehicle
meanings.internalScope: Leaving a bounded area by transport. z+Genitive realizes a selected source role, not exclusive government. Excludes destination, vehicle, route, time, and manner. No syntax is borrowed from imperfective wyjeżdżać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For the place you are leaving, use z + Genitive: wyjadę z miasta (I'll leave the city). This does not name a destination.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep the exact imperfective identity and Accusative object; do not author a Dative recipient or inherit any construction from przynieść.

meanings.internalScope: Physically carrying or bringing a thing to a destination. Direct Accusative names the carried object. Optional generalized source/goal roles exist in the sense but no concrete preposition realization is authored for product use. No Dative recipient exists; that Phase 2 hypothesis was explicitly rejected. No syntax is inherited from perfective przynieść.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you bring takes the Accusative: przynoszę kawę (I'm bringing coffee).

bindingConstraints.text: Author the exact answer sense with alternative na-question and że-content schemas; exclude an unverified Dative person and unrelated meanings.

meanings.internalScope: Answering a question or prior utterance by speaking. na+Accusative names the question/content target; że introduces a content clause; direct speech may also express the answer's content. These are alternatives, not a combined maximal frame. No Dative addressee exists; the person spoken to is not a schema position. Matching/preference, correspondence, and other odpowiadać senses are excluded.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For what you're answering, use na + Accusative: odpowiadam na pytanie (I'm answering the question).
Use że to introduce the content of your answer: odpowiadam, że nie wiem (I answer that I don't know).
You can also give the answer's exact words directly: odpowiadam: „Nie wiem” (I answer: "I don't know").

examples.en: I answer that I don't know.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep beneficiary schemas alternative, label u + Genitive as a realization rather than exclusive provider government, and do not build a maximal frame.

meanings.internalScope: Ordering or commissioning something for payment. Accusative names the ordered item. Dative and dla+Genitive are alternative beneficiary realizations of the same participant, not combined into one frame. u+Genitive is a documented realization of a selected provider/location role, not exclusive provider government. No syntax is borrowed from perfective zamówić.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you order takes the Accusative: zamawiam pizzę (I'm ordering a pizza).
To say who the order is for, one way is the Dative: zamawiam mężowi prezent (I'm ordering a present for my husband).
Another way to say who the order is for is dla + Genitive: zamawiam prezent dla żony (I'm ordering a present for my wife).
One common way to name the provider is u + Genitive: zamawiam meble u stolarza (I'm ordering furniture from a carpenter).

examples.en: I am ordering a present for my husband.
I am ordering a present for my wife.
I am ordering furniture from a carpenter.

meanings.internalScope: Bounded onset of an activity. Accusative names the activity as a direct object; infinitive names the action begun. Both are independently evidenced for perfective zacząć; no syntax is inherited from the metadata-only imperfective partner zaczynać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The activity you start takes the Accusative: zacząłem lekcję (I started the lesson).
Use an infinitive to say what you started doing: zacząłem czytać książkę (I started reading a book).

meanings.internalScope: Bringing an activity or task to its end. Accusative names the activity/task; the infinitive is selected, naming the action being finished, not a purpose adjunct. Exact imperfective kończyć is independently evidenced; no syntax is borrowed from perfective skończyć, and this record does not pre-decide the later kończyć/skończyć pair policy.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The task you finish takes the Accusative: kończę pracę (I'm finishing the work).
Use an infinitive to say what you're finishing doing: kończę czytać książkę (I'm finishing reading the book).

examples.en: I am finishing reading the book.

meanings.internalScope: Recalling or retaining people, things, events, or information. Direct Accusative names the remembered person/thing/event/information; o+Locative names a remembered topic. Independently verified że-content-clause and interrogative-dependent-clause constructions also exist in this exact sense but are intentionally not authored in this record; see the Batch 2 risk report for the omission rationale. Excludes the distinct obligation/reminder meaning and does not use żeby.

Remembering that an action should be performed; an obligation/reminder sense distinct from ordinary recall. Infinitive and żeby-clause are both selected. Not merged into recall merely because English can translate both with 'remember'; does not use że or o+Locative.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you remember takes the Accusative: pamiętam ten dzień (I remember that day).
For a remembered topic, use o + Locative: pamiętam o twoich urodzinach (I remember your birthday).
Use an infinitive when you and the person doing the action are the same: pamiętaj zamknąć drzwi (remember to close the door).
Use żeby when the person who should act is different: pamiętaj, żeby dzieci umyły ręce (remember that the children should wash their hands).

examples.en: Remember that the children should wash their hands.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep recall and failure-to-act senses separate and omit the unverified żeby schema.

meanings.internalScope: Losing recall of people, things, events, or information. Direct Genitive and direct Accusative both realize the remembered/forgotten object; o+Locative names a remembered topic; że and czy content clauses realize forgotten propositional/question content. All are directly verified for this exact sense. Excludes the distinct failure-to-act meaning below and does not use żeby; that schema was explicitly rejected by Phase 3.

glossesEn: fail to do something one should have done
meanings.internalScope: Failing to perform an action that should have been performed. Infinitive is the sole authorized construction. The proposed żeby-clause was explicitly rejected by Phase 3 evidence and must not be authored here. No syntax is inherited from another aspect identity; this meaning is kept separate from the recall/forgetting sense above.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The forgotten thing can take the Genitive: zapominam numeru telefonu (I forget the phone number).
The forgotten thing can also take the Accusative: zapominam tę twarz (I forget that face).
For a forgotten topic, use o + Locative: zapominam o spotkaniu (I forget about the meeting).
Use że to introduce what you forget: zapominam, że mam spotkanie (I forget that I have a meeting).
Use czy to introduce a forgotten yes/no question: zapominam, czy zamknąłem drzwi (I forget whether I locked the door).
Use an infinitive to say the action you failed to do: zapominam zadzwonić (I forget to call).

examples.en: I forget that I have a meeting.
I forget whether I locked the door.

bindingConstraints.text: Author the listed alternative schemas separately; do not freely combine Dative, na + Accusative, infinitive, and żeby positions or transfer participants across senses.
Author direct Genitive only and omit infinitive government.

phase3Evidence.primarySourceLocator: single lexical entry; Definicja, Połączenia, Składnia

bindingConstraints.text: Label w + Locative as a residence-place realization rather than exclusive government; restrict z + Instrumental to the selected co-resident role.
Preserve lexical się, keep appointment and agreement senses separate, label do as a realization, and do not merge alternatives into a maximal frame.
Label do/na targets as realizations, retain direct content clauses, and do not encode w sprawie + Genitive as a governed construction.
